parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the trend in volatility of the halogens chlorine, bromine and iodine. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Iodine is made by reacting bromine with sodium iodide.
parts.text: Construct an ionic equation for the reaction of bromine with sodium iodide.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the role of bromine in the reaction. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: Concentrated sulfuric acid is added to separate samples containing equal amounts of $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{NaBr}$ and $\text{NaI}$. All three samples initially react to produce the hydrogen halide.
parts.text: Write an equation to describe the acid-base reaction that occurs when concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with $\text{NaBr}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce which sodium halide, $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{NaBr}$ or $\text{NaI}$, produces the largest percentage yield of hydrogen halide when concentrated sulfuric acid is added. Explain your answer by considering the relative reactivity of the halide ions as reducing agents.
